Why You Need Ongoing CCTV Maintenance & AMC

AA CCTV system is only as useful as its coverage and its footage — cameras pointed at the wrong angle, recording at too low a resolution, or storing footage for a shorter period than ADMCC and SIRA retention standards require all quietly defeat the purpose of having the system at all. It's easy to end up with a system that looks complete on paper — a certain number of cameras, a recorder, a monitor — but still fails when it actually matters, or fails an ADMCC/MCC compliance inspection, because the one angle that mattered wasn't covered or the footage was already overwritten by the time anyone went looking for it.

Most of the problems we see with existing CCTV systems trace back to the planning stage, not the equipment — and to skipping regular CCTV maintenance once the system goes live. A camera mounted too high loses facial detail. A camera facing a doorway with strong backlight from outside washes out into a silhouette. Storage sized for a week of footage doesn't help when an incident isn't reported until ten days later, and a recorder that hasn't been checked in months can quietly stop saving footage without anyone noticing. None of these are equipment failures — they're planning failures and missed CCTV AMC checks, and they're avoidable if the system is designed around how the property actually gets used and kept compliant with MCC, ADMCC, and SIRA requirements through ongoing maintenance, not just installed once and left alone.

As an ADMCC-approved CCTV installer in Abu Dhabi and SIRA-compliant provider in Dubai, we design and install both IP and analog camera systems across Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, and Al Ain, planning camera placement and coverage around the actual layout and risk areas of each property — not a generic camera count. That means walking the site, identifying entry points, blind spots, and the areas where footage would actually matter if something happened, then specifying camera type, angle, resolution, and storage duration to match. It's also why our work doesn't stop at installation — every system we design is backed by ongoing CCTV maintenance and AMC options, so the system holds up long after installation day, not just when it's new.
our services
CCTV System Design

Every CCTV installation starts with a site walkthrough to identify entry points, blind spots, and high-priority areas — parking, entrances, loading bays, cash handling points — before deciding on camera type, placement, and count. We specify a mix of fixed, dome, bullet, and PTZ (pan-tilt-zoom) cameras depending on what each area actually needs, rather than installing the same camera type across an entire property regardless of coverage requirements.
CCTV Camera Installation

Our technicians install cameras, run cabling, and configure the recording system — NVR or DVR depending on whether the cameras are IP or analog — so the finished system records reliably from day one. Cabling is routed and secured properly rather than run as a temporary-looking mess of exposed wire, and every camera is tested for image quality and coverage angle before we consider the job complete.
CCTV Maintenance

A CCTV system that isn't maintained tends to fail quietly — a camera goes out of focus, a cable connection loosens, storage fills up and starts overwriting footage sooner than expected, and nobody notices until the footage is actually needed and isn't there. We provide scheduled CCTV maintenance, checking camera image quality, cabling and connections, recording storage, and overall system function, so the system is actually working when it matters, not just installed and left alone.
Remote Monitoring & Access

Most CCTV systems we install support remote viewing, so property owners and facility managers can check live or recorded footage from a phone or computer without being on-site. We configure remote access securely, so footage is viewable when needed without leaving the system exposed to unauthorized access over the internet.

blocks.text: Choosing the Right CCTV Camera

The right camera comes down to two decisions: IP (network) or analog, and which camera type suits where it's mounted. IP cameras generally offer higher resolution, easier remote access, and more flexible storage, while analog systems can be a lower-cost option for simpler coverage needs. Within either, options include bullet, dome, PTZ (pan-tilt-zoom), and specialized cameras for particular surveillance requirements.

Factors such as lighting conditions, viewing distance, indoor or outdoor installation, required image detail, storage requirements, and network infrastructure all affect which setup — and what it costs — is right for your property, whether it's a home, villa, or commercial site. We assess these factors during a site visit and recommend the right mix rather than a one-size camera count.
